test_title: PYST 1: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:12 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The students have presented national level projects to the jury successfully.

options.text: National level projects had been presented by the students to the jury successfully.
National level projects were presented by the students to the jury successfully.
National level projects have been presented by the students to the jury successfully.
National level projects have presented by the students to the jury successfully.

solution:
The correct answer is:** 'National level projects have been presented by the students to the jury successfully'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct option of the Active to Passive is:** 'National level projects have been presented by the students to the jury successfully'.**
 
• The given sentence is in **'Present Perfect Tense'. **The structure of it is: **'Subject + Have/ Has + V3 (Past Participle of the verb) + Object'.**
 
• While changing it active to passive, 'the subject' (**The students**) will be 'Object' and the 'Object' (**national level projects**) will be the 'subject' and 'verb' will be placed according to 'the Subject' (If it is singular, singular verb will be used. If it is plural, plural verb will be used).
 
• In Passive voice, **'Subject + have/ has + been + V3 + by + Object'** will be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'National level projects had been presented by the students to the jury successfully'** is not correct here.
 
• **'National level projects were presented by the students to the jury successfully'** is not correct here.
 
• **'National level projects have presented by the students to the jury successfully'** is not correct here.
